transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um... well, my wife and my director at work kind of insisted I come in. I guess... I've just been starting a lot of things lately. Projects. 

Like, uh, new work plans, scheduling certifications, upgrading the home network... messaging old contacts. It just... gets pretty intense, I guess. I kind of just keep going until one of them has to step in and tell me I've gone past normal limits.
During this time when you've been starting all these projects, how much sleep have you been getting, and do you feel like you need less sleep than usual?

Um... not a lot, I suppose. There have been runs where I... maybe sleep three hours. I just wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m. 

I don't really feel tired, though. It just kind of feels like I've been handed bonus time. So I just use it.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt very low, depressed, or down for several days or weeks at a time?

Yeah... I guess so. There are, um... stretches where I just feel... really flat. Heavy, I guess. I wake up and just feel like... like a failed version of myself. Even just answering my wife when she asks a normal question... it just feels like too much effort. So, yeah. I have those times too.
During these times when you're starting lots of projects and sleeping very little, how long do these periods typically last—are we talking days, weeks, or longer?

Um... weeks, usually. I don't really keep track of the exact days. 

But I guess these... stretches, where I'm just going and not sleeping much... they've been a part of my life for a while now. Roughly a year and eight months, maybe.
When you have those stretches where you feel really flat and heavy, how long do those typically last—are we talking days, weeks, or longer?

Um... longer, I guess. Weeks... sometimes more. 

If I had to add it all up... all those heavy times over the last year and a half or so... maybe it's been around seven months total. Just... being like that.

During those heavy, flat periods you mentioned—when you're feeling like a failed version of yourself and everything feels like too much effort—have you ever experienced things like feeling worthless, having thoughts about harming yourself, or difficulty concentrating during those times?

Um... I don't really have thoughts about hurting myself. But... the worthless feeling, yeah. I guess I get that. 

I just... I manage IT systems, and we had a migration recently. During those heavy times, I just keep replaying these really small mistakes from the migration. It gets to where I start feeling like I let down the whole department... and my family... even the students I mentor. Just... way beyond what probably makes sense. But... yeah. That happens.
During those weeks when you're feeling flat and heavy, do you remember the shortest one of those periods—was it at least two weeks long, or sometimes shorter than that?
Um... I don't really know. I don't keep a calendar of it. They just... happen. I couldn't tell you the exact number of days.
When you're in one of those heavy, flat periods, do you think the shortest one has lasted at least two weeks, or do they sometimes come and go faster than that?

I... I think I mentioned it a minute ago. If you add up all those low, withdrawn times... it comes out to about seven months total. I don't really track if one was exactly two weeks or not. It just... adds up to that much.

When you're in one of those heavy, flat periods, can you think back to one specific time—like maybe the most recent one—and try to remember roughly how many days or weeks that one lasted before you started feeling better?
Um... the most recent one... I guess it was a while. Maybe a few weeks? I don't really know. It's hard to keep track when everything just feels... heavy. I didn't really count the days.

I understand it's hard to keep track of exact days. But thinking about one of those heavy, flat periods—even just your best guess—do you think the shortest one lasted at least two weeks, or could some of them have been shorter than that?
I don't know... I really don't. It's just... it's a blur. I guess some could have been shorter. Or longer. I just... I can't be sure.
I know it's hard to remember exactly, but thinking back over the past year or so—have you ever had one of those heavy, flat periods that you're pretty sure lasted less than two weeks?

I... I really don't know about the exact weeks. I just know that if you put all those low, withdrawn times together... it's been about seven months total since this all started. I can't break it down more than that.

When you're in one of those heavy, flat periods, and you start to feel better—like when that heavy feeling begins to lift—roughly how many days pass from when it starts until you begin to feel that shift? Are we talking about something that happens over days, or does it take weeks?
I... I really couldn't say. Like I said, it's just a blur. I don't know if it's days or weeks. I just don't know.

I know you've said it's hard to track exact days, but let me ask it differently: when you're in one of those heavy, flat periods, and you're at your worst—feeling that heaviness most intensely—does that worst part usually last for at least a couple of weeks, or does it sometimes feel like it comes and goes more quickly than that?

I... I just don't know how to answer that. I can't break it down into a couple of weeks here or there. I just know... if you add it all up, all those heavy times... it's been about seven months total. That's all I know.

When you're feeling that heavy, flat way—at your absolute worst with that feeling—has there ever been a time when you felt that way for several days in a row, and then it lifted, all within just one week or less?

I... look, I don't know how else to say it. I don't track the days like that. Like I already told you... if you just take all those low, withdrawn times and put them together... it adds up to about seven months. I really can't give you exact weeks or days.
You mentioned the most recent heavy, flat period was a while ago. Is that one still going on right now, or did it end?

Yeah. It's... still going on. I just wake up feeling like... I don't know, like a failed version of myself. It's just heavy and flat. Even if my wife just asks me a normal question, it... it feels like too much to even answer. So, no, it hasn't ended.
I know you said it's hard to track exact days, but let me ask this simply: how many weeks ago did this current heavy, flat feeling that you're experiencing right now actually start?

I... I really don't know. I can't give you a number of weeks for this specific time. Like I keep saying, I just don't track it that way. I just know that over this whole thing... if you add up all the low, withdrawn periods... it's about seven months total. That's... that's all I have.

You said this current heavy, flat feeling is still going on right now. Setting aside all the other low periods you've had—just focusing on this one that started at some point and is still happening now—has it been going on for at least 2 weeks continuously, or less than that?
I... I guess it's been at least two weeks. Probably more. I don't know exactly when it started, but... yeah, it's been a while.

Since this current heavy, flat feeling started—even though you're not sure exactly when—has there been any time during it where you felt noticeably better or back to your normal self, even for a few days? Or has it been pretty continuously heavy and flat the whole time?

No... not really. It's... it's just been like I said. Just continuously heavy. I don't really get days where I wake up feeling normal right now. It's just... that same feeling of being a failure, where even talking to my wife is too much. It hasn't let up.

During these past 7 months or so when you've had those low, heavy periods—have you had any times in between where you went back to that high energy state, starting lots of projects and not sleeping much? Or has it mostly been low periods with maybe just short breaks in between?

Yeah... there were times like that. I guess... if I really look back over the last couple of years, those high-energy phases... the pressured ones... they've actually taken up more time than the down periods. Or even the quiet times in between. So... yeah.

During this current heavy, flat period that's been going on for at least a couple of weeks—have you had any days where you suddenly felt more energized, or where you had that racing mind and wanted to start new projects again, even if just for a day or two? Or has it stayed consistently heavy and flat the whole time?
No... it's just been flat. I haven't had any energy at all.
